_comment: The ratio of valgebra to pydantic's strict TypeAdapter each shape must stay under: a claim the project makes, not a measurement it recorded. The argument for the ceilings, for the recorded block beside them and for the one shape excluded from it is docs/dev/07-tooling-ci.md, under 'The competitive ratio' -- a page the documentation lint reads and this file is not. Changing a ceiling or re-recording a ratio is an edit with an argument in its commit message; scripts/perf_gate.py --against is the fine-grained gate.
_free_threaded_comment: Ceilings the free-threaded build is held to instead, for the shapes where it is a different performance environment rather than the same one on a slower clock. A shape absent from here is held to the shared ceiling above. Reading an element out of a list takes the list's lock there, and a shape whose cost is per-element pays it; docs/11-performance.md measures that and says which shapes part.
_recorded_comment: The ratio each shape last measured, the spread it was measured across, and the environment both belong to. See docs/dev/07-tooling-ci.md for why a claim alone stopped being enough.

unratcheted.error_report: Not measurable on this instrument. Five runs of one PGO CPython 3.12 build read 0.861, 0.882, 0.889, 1.056 and 1.193 -- a spread of 0.33, a third of the shape's own value, where every other shape spreads between 0.001 and 0.048. Twelve runs of another PGO CPython 3.12 build read 0.43 to 0.46 (docs/11-performance.md), so the spread is the build's as much as the shape's. A tolerance wide enough not to fire on that noise would be wider than any regression worth catching, and a tighter one would fire constantly. The shape keeps its ceiling of 1.60, which it is nowhere near crossing, and the reason it is noisy is worth its own reading: it is the only shape timing a path that raises and formats an exception, so a Python exception's cost is inside the measurement.

recorded._how_to_arm: Unrecorded on a measurement. A recording made off the bench lane would match its fingerprint while carrying another machine's noise, and one made on it is one run on one of the lane's two classes of machine: three runs of one commit read scalar 0.156, 0.197 and 0.159, and one commit's push read deep_nesting 0.165 where its dispatch read 0.124 and 0.126, each pair further apart than the shape's tolerance. A ratio recorded from one run fires on the next run that lands on the other class, with nothing changed. What arms the ratchet is a ratio that is a figure of the lane, with a tolerance read from the same readings; docs/dev/07-tooling-ci.md gives the lane's spread. The tolerances below cover the shapes' own spread on CPython 3.14 read twice on one box: twelve runs of a PGO wheel on uv's build and eighteen on a source build. Each is at least the wider of the two, rounded up (scalar 0.021, large_array 0.010, deep_nesting 0.023, wide_record 0.022, json_document 0.058, build 0.001).
